#2817. Rams PFF grades: Offensive line pancakes Chargers in win

The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 24-9 to move to 4-4 on the season.

The Rams have two winnable games on deck against the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals to potentially put together a four-game win streak and move to 6-4.

But before we get ahead of ourselves, let's put a cap on the team's win over the Chargers. These are the Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades from the game with important notes.

PFF counted four pressures on Matthew Stafford across 26 dropbacks. The quarterback was sacked only a single time. The offensive line was credited with only one of these pressures, which suggests Stafford was inviting pressure with his play.

Steve Avila did not allow a single pressure. He was also effective in the run game with a grade of 82.9.

Dotson also did not allow a pressure. He posted a run grade of 79.9. This was by far his best grade of the season, which is encouraging because he has not looked like himself. Dotson has strung together two positive performances and could be trending in the right direction.

The offense runs through Puka Nacua. He caught 11 of 12 targets for 80 yards with a score. 65 of his yards came after the catch point, and he averaged nearly six additional yards per catch. With a 1.5 average depth of target (ADOT), Nacua was doing the hard work for nearly every yard he gained.

Shelton received a poor pass protection grade of 57.5 with no pressures allowed. He shined in the run game at 79.5.

McClendon is the only lineman to allow a pressure. Still, he finished with a strong pass protection grade of 70.8 with even better marks in the run game at 74.6.

The Rams had 110 yards after the catch point in the passing game. Matthew Stafford had 157 passing yards on the day. Just 30% of his yardage total on the game were "air yards", which underscores how suffocated the passing game felt at times. Stafford finished with an ADOT of just 3.8 yards down field with a 2.26 second time to throw. That is about as short and fast as it gets.

McDuffie intercepted Justin Herbert and nearly returned for a defensive scheme. He made five defensive run stops from the secondary with nine total tackles. Herbert looked his way often with eight targets. McDuffie allowed six receptions for 47 yards, of which 45 came after the catch with a long of 30.

Speights' best work came this week in pass coverage with a grade of 91.5. He allowed three catches on four targets for 14 yards.

Nate Landman is still the starter in the middle of the defense. He played 42 snaps, and that suggests his role as an every-down player is diminishing. Quentin Lake was the "green d0t" guy. Speights played 35 snaps.

The interior defensive line continues to step up without Poona Ford and Kobie Turner. Tyler Davis was the emerging player this week, and he ranked third on the defense in run grade behind McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. He also added two pressures as a pass rusher.

Lake snatched the first of two Justin Herbert interceptions on the day. In total he allowed three catches on four targets for 30 yards. Lake did not miss a tackle on six attempts. He rushed the passer on three occasions.

Jaylen Watson suffered a shoulder injury and played 41 of the total 61 defensive snaps. Forbes was the biggest recipient of this additional playing time with 17 snaps. The corner was targeted one time and allowed just one catch for a yard, including five yards after the catch.

Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, and Byron Young were the three lowest graded defenders this week at 54.9, 53.1, and 49.7, respectively. That doesn't happen often. It's still encouraging that someone other than the usual suspects stepped up in a stifling defensive performance.

#2815. Hawks escape six-man Pacers 108–104 after record-tying first half

The Atlanta Hawks escaped with a 108–104 victory over an Indiana Pacers team with just six available players Monday, surviving a late rally behind Nickeil Alexander-Walker's 34 points.

Alexander-Walker connected on nine of his 15 three-point attempts. CJ McCollum finished one rebound shy of a triple-double with 13 points, 12 assists and nine rebounds, while Onyeka Okongwu contributed 13 points and 10 rebounds.

Atlanta made 15 three-pointers before halftime, tying the franchise record for any half. However, its hot shooting gave way to a stagnant offense after the break, allowing the depleted Pacers to fight their way back.

The Hawks were also missing key players, with Jalen Johnson sidelined by a left ankle sprain and Kingston Flemings serving a one-game suspension. Still, against an Indiana team operating with such limited personnel, Atlanta made the finish considerably harder than it needed to be.

The opening quarter offered little indication of those later struggles. Atlanta shot 60 percent from the field and 70 percent from three-point range, establishing an early offensive rhythm.

Rookie Zuby Ejiofor also made his regular-season debut, connecting from beyond the arc for his first NBA basket.

The Hawks maintained control through the second quarter, although Indiana showed the persistence that kept it competitive throughout the night. An 11–2 Pacers run cut the deficit to single digits, but Atlanta continued making perimeter shots to finish its record-tying half.

After halftime, those shots stopped falling as consistently. Atlanta led by as many as 15 points, but Indiana put together a 7–0 third-quarter run to help trim the deficit to five.

The Hawks' ball movement stalled, leaving them with stagnant possessions against a more active Pacers defense. Indiana outscored Atlanta 23–19 in the quarter, setting up a competitive finish.

Atlanta continued leaving the door open in the fourth. Fouls gave the Pacers opportunities at the free-throw line, while a late 9–0 Indiana run made it a one-possession game.

The Hawks ultimately held on, but the result did little to erase concerns about their second-half execution. Alexander-Walker's shooting and McCollum's playmaking helped secure the victory, yet Atlanta struggled to sustain the offensive flow needed to put away its opponent.

Indiana deserves credit for its effort. Despite having only six players available, the Pacers continued competing, increased their defensive pressure and gave themselves a chance to win late.

For Atlanta, the victory was welcome, but the performance left plenty to address. A record-tying shooting half should have provided the foundation for a more controlled finish. Instead, the Hawks needed to survive a final push from a severely shorthanded opponent.

The Hawks next face the Washington Wizards on Wednesday, hoping to have Jalen Johnson and Jock Landale back in the lineup.

#2814. Joshua Buatsi Could Be In Trouble Against Willy Hutchinson—and Here's Why

On Saturday night at the AO Arena in Manchester, England, we'll see a rematch between Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson. Their first fight was one of the best fights we saw in 2024.

The scorecards were pretty wide in favor of Buatsi, but if you saw the fight, you know it was closer than that appears. Those wide scorecards were due in part to the two knockdowns Buatsi scored against Hutchinson.

One of the three judges actually scored it 113–112 for Hutchinson, while the other two had it 117–108 and 115–110 for Buatsi.

No matter, their rematch will be for the vacant WBC light heavyweight title, and it will headline a DAZN card on November 7.

Buatsi 20-1 (13 KOs), Hutchinson 20-2 (14 KOs)

The first fight took place at Wembley Stadium in September 2024 on the Anthony Joshua-Daniel Dubois undercard, with the interim WBO title at stake. Buatsi dropped Hutchinson with a right hand in the sixth round and again with a body shot late in the ninth.

The rematch was first sanctioned for the WBC's interim title. It became a fight for the full belt after David Benavidez vacated it ahead of his Dec. 5 cruiserweight unification fight with Michal Cieslak.

This rematch is going to be interesting because, since their first fight, Buatsi has taken what I think is a considerable amount of damage.

He suffered a loss to Callum Smith, and he's had at least one other fight that could have impacted him in the long term.

Being a fighter who has participated in so many wars makes you wonder if this is the fight where we actually see him take a step back.

Because of that, some people may believe Willy Hutchinson has an opportunity to gain the edge in this rematch.

Buatsi is tough as nails, and Hutchinson isn't known for his punching power. So this is a fight I can see going the distance.

However, I can see Hutchinson having more left in the tank, outboxing Buatsi, and winning this fight by decision.

#2809. Georgia’s NIL Arms Race Is Here to Stay. Rick Jackson Has a Plan to Fix it.

ATHENS — Georgia football is no longer competing only on the recruiting trail.

The Bulldogs are competing in a rapidly changing college sports economy. Name, image and likeness opportunities, direct athlete compensation and revenue sharing have changed how major programs build rosters.

Georgia has the resources, brand recognition and alumni network to remain a national contender. The challenge is organizing those advantages into a sustainable operation.

UGA already operates an official NIL program. Its Georgia Bulldogs Exchange platform connects student-athletes with potential business partners. The athletic department also provides branding education and tools to help athletes pursue opportunities.

The House settlement has added another layer of complexity. Athletic departments must balance athlete compensation, recruiting, compliance, donor relationships and traditional operating expenses.

That is where Georgia's business community could become especially valuable.

Rick Jackson's background as a healthcare entrepreneur gives him a business perspective that could be relevant to discussions about the state's broader sports economy. Any meaningful proposal, however, would need to explain exactly how state leadership could support UGA without interfering with university governance or NCAA and conference rules.

There are practical questions worth asking.

Could Georgia make it easier for local businesses to partner with athletes? Could state leaders help strengthen relationships between universities and major employers? Could the state create a more attractive environment for companies looking to invest in Georgia sports?

Those conversations matter because NIL is not going away.

Georgia cannot afford to treat the new college athletics economy as a temporary inconvenience. The Bulldogs need a professional approach that protects the program's competitive position while supporting athletes and maintaining responsible financial practices.

The next era of Georgia football will require more than recruiting stars. It will require smart business relationships, disciplined management and a willingness to adapt.

#2806. The NFL, Caleb Williams shoe dispute takes center stage on Monday night

Monday night’s game between the Bears and Seahawks in Seattle comes with a subplot. Other than the ongoing Joe Buck and Troy Aikman drama.

The league has twice fined Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams for displaying an “unauthorized logo” (i.e., “the logo of a company that doesn’t pay us”) on his shoes. After the Week 6 game against the Falcons, the league fined Williams $11,941. After the Week 7 game against the Patriots, the league fined Williams $23,882 — twice the amount of the first fine.

Williams has said he will continue to wear the Caddix cleats, citing safety considerations. Unlike most if not all other NFL players who use Caddix footwear, Williams declines to cover the identifying markings with tape.

While the controversy calls back to former Bears quarterback Jim McMahon’s battles with the league over his Adidas headband during a playoff game (after being fined $5,000, he went with “ROZELLE” for the NFC Championship and “POW-MIA” for the Super Bowl) and to Bears linebacker Brian Urlacher’s whopping $100,000 fine for wearing a VitaminWater hat to Super Bowl XLI media day, Williams’s choice of footwear is rooted in the basic belief that the shoes promote player safety.

As to the refusal to cover the shoes with tape to hide the Caddix markings, it’s unclear whether he’s concerned about undermining the performance of the shoe or whether he’s simply trying to prove a point.

The NFL is clearly trying to prove a point, by fining him repeatedly. And while both prior fines are pending on appeal, a third fine is inevitable unless Williams bends.

Regardless, the next chapter arrives tonight. Neither of the fine letters threaten Williams with preventing him from playing if he doesn’t tape over the logos and markings. If the league decides to do that, Williams will have a pretty big decision to make.

Coach Ben Johnson was asked about that possible outcome on Saturday. “He’s all about the team, and I know he’s not going to hurt the team,” Johnson said.

The question of whether Johnson would be “hurting the team” is a matter of perspective. Williams wouldn’t be “hurting the team” by refusing to play; the NFL would be “hurting the team” by refusing to let Williams play in his preferred shoes.

Either way, both sides have been stubborn. It seems that a compromise could be reached, somehow.

#2800. INTERVIEW: Rouven Kasper on Bayern's Kenya excursion in 2027 and tapping into African and South American markets

Having recently announced plans to visit Kenya in January for a mid-season tour and game against Ajax, Bayern Munich's Chief Marketing & Sales officer Rouven Kasper believes the club are expanding their popularity in Africa.

"It's a wonderful opportunity for us to be playing there. We have been focusing on the continent [Africa] in recent months," Kasper explained to Bulinews.com and other media present regarding their 5 January 2027 trip to Nairobi.

"We acquired, together with our Red and Gold initiative, a very strong academy in Ghana, Senegal and Cameroon. Knowing that Bara [Sapoko Ndiaye] is from one of these academies, from an athletic perspective it's very relevant.

"As well as playing the match, opening what will be a very big stadium and playing there [in Nairobi, Kenya] in the pre-season against Ajax Amsterdam, it's a perfect combination which everyone is looking forward to," he added.

Elaborating on his point, Kasper feels there a multitude of reasons as to why a club like the German record champions are sought after. It ranges from what happens on the pitch to the accessibility of players off it.

"I think generally when it comes to football, people look to the top clubs and we are one of the most successful in the world. If you look at UEFA's coefficient over the last 10 years, we rank as the best.

"We play lovely football, we are successful and I think people like that we are approachable. An example is our summer tours where the players are very approachable, not just flying in and flying out.

"We are there and we invest strongly into the interpersonal relationship [in these countries] by giving back to the people. In the end, football is from the people and fore the people – it's a special thing that we focus on this.

"Maybe as well, it's based on the German DNA – [to be] very reliable, it's based on quality and whatever we do you can count on us. There, we have a positive difference compared to others.

"We haven't been to Africa that often, so we need to learn as well. Learn from what we experience there, our fans there, and talking with them," Kasper said, highlighting that this is more than purely a ploy for financial gain.

South American markets, Kasper explains, have also been extremely kind towards the Bavarian giants in recent years. Namely Colombia with former and current stars James Rodríguez and Luis Díaz donning the red jersey.

"Generally, the numbers in the Americas [North and South] are growing very fast. James Rodríguez, already with his amazing followers, is still in the top four for followers [for a South American footballer] which is very impressive.

"Having Luis Díaz with us now, for Colombia as an example, is also impressive. Only looking at our social media followers in Colombia, they have grown over 500 percent. Brazil is also growing very fast too.

"This is because we as the Bundesliga together are focusing there [South America] for socials with lots of content. The content is just wonderful and there is a wonderful passion there for sure.

"Not all Germans speak Spanish; we have a disadvantage in language, but we have the same passion in us playing football. We are seeing that the numbers are increasing for viewership of Bundesliga matches and out social media.

"Our merchandising is also increasing. In this part of the world, it is also very positive [in terms of sales], so people are demanding it which is positive. Hopefully it will continue on like this," he concluded.

#2787. No. 21 USC cruises past Milwaukee in season-opening blowout

LOS ANGELES – The 2026-2027 season for USC basketball is officially underway. It began with an emphatic 95-63 victory over the Milwaukee Panthers on Monday night at the Galen Center, providing the first glimpse of a revamped Trojans roster.

Expectations have certainly been raised for the program this year after an offseason spent compiling some of the most notable transfer and recruiting classes in the nation. Their seven-man transfer class was ranked fourth in the country by On3, while ESPN ranked their recruiting class No. 7.

USC enters the season ranked No. 21, marking both its first preseason national ranking and highest ranking at any point under head coach Eric Musselman.

"[I'm] impressed with some things we did from an offensive standpoint, like shooting the three, and super impressed with our two freshmen in the Ratliffs," Musselman said. "But we got a lot of things to clean up as far as taking care of the basketball. We've got to play better in transition."

Coaching his 12th collegiate season, he improved to 11-1 in season openers and 3-0 with the Trojans.

From the jump, they were given a nice boost from guard Alijah Arenas. The sophomore, who appeared in just 14 games last season, helped USC open up a quick 10-5 lead as he contributed four points, two rebounds and a steal.

Arenas continued to make an impact the rest of the way, putting together a well-rounded performance. He finished with 21 points on 9-of-14 shooting to lead all guards, adding eight rebounds, two assists and two steals.

"It was amazing," Arenas said when asked about being available for the season opener. "It's a blessing that I got to have a full offseason. I'm just all around very excited to play. I have no complaints here for anything whatsoever."

Meanwhile, the highly-regarded freshman big man twins, Adonis and Darius Ratliff, were exactly as advertised in their regular-season collegiate debuts. Adonis led all scorers, posting 25 points on 7-of-10 shooting (5-of-7 from three). It was the most points by a USC freshman in his debut since O.J. Mayo in 2007.

USC Trojans forward Adonis Ratliff (3) attempts a free throw during a game against the Milwaukee Panthers on Monday, November 2, 2026, at Galen Center in Los Angeles, California.

USC Trojans forward Adonis Ratliff (3) attempts a free throw during a game against the Milwaukee Panthers on Monday, November 2, 2026, at Galen Center in Los Angeles, California.

The 7-footer was just as imposing physically, grabbing six rebounds, blocking two shots and collecting two steals.

Darius was just as effective and equally as trigger-happy with the basketball in his hands. He finished 5-of-10 from the field (1-of-1 from three) for 14 total points, adding two rebounds, two assists and sending away five shots on the defensive end.

"Their shot selection [has] been really good," Musselman said. "Behind closed doors in practice, it's been good in the exhibition games, it was good tonight. When Adonis gets his feet set, he's as good a shooter as…in the two and a half years now that I've been here that we've had."

It should be no secret after Monday's performance that the twins, one of eight sets in college basketball, are going to play a substantial role in the Trojans' success. Their height and shooting ability will only continue to serve as matchup nightmares for opposing defenses.

"My first college experience was definitely eye-opening," Darius said. "We played a couple exhibition games, but we saw that there were certain things we need to work on. We just got in the lab, worked on it…just came out and produced."

Guard Rodney Rice, who elected to return for his senior year after playing in just six games last season, distributed the ball nicely to form a cohesive backcourt duo with Arenas. Rice added 15 points of his own, while his nine assists were just one short of a career high.

"I thought in the first half, he was almost a little too unselfish," Musselman said. "I didn't think he really looked to score. Obviously, the nine assists, that's a large number, especially the way that he can score the basketball. So, I thought he played really well."

KJ Lewis, coming from Arizona this offseason as one of the Trojans' transfer additions, scored 10 points on 4-of-5 shooting in 23 minutes. He also provided two assists, a rebound and a steal.

While it was a mostly successful night for USC, the squad will have to monitor the status of junior forward Jacob Cofie, who exited the game in the first half and did not return. Musselman described him as dealing with "severe back spasms" and said he is concerned about Cofie's potential availability against Wichita State on Sunday.

Sunday's battle against the Shockers will take place in Nevada at the Tahoe Blue Event Center as part of the Caesars Lake Tahoe Classic.

After Reese's loss in the 2026 WNBA Finals, her mother announced her return to social media with a message for the opponents.

Reese scored eight points and grabbed 12 rebounds in the final game, but shot only 3-for-7 and turned the ball over four times. Her finals run saw inconsistent play after a string of three good games. Reese's mom, Angel Webb Reese, might have wished to return to X with her daughter's win, but the tables turned.

"I'm back on this app after 6 months & Congratulations to the @valkyries on winning the 26′ 🏆!"

Reese would have been up for the Finals MVP award if she had won one more game for the Dream, but in the end, Gabby Williams had the honor. The Valkyries took Game 7 68-63 as the French forward scored 30 points and blocked four shots. The Dream will go back to the drawing board and see how they can improve next season.

Angel Reese wasn't dejected when the Dream couldn't go and win the title after taking the series to Game 7:

"I am beyond proud and have absolutely nothing to hang my head about. Every loss is a lesson, and sometimes it's not NO, just NOT YET. Delayed, not denied. Trust me. I'm hungry for more."

The Dream had DeWanna Bonner's services, but that couldn't help the team get past the Valkyries' defensive fortress. Reese struggled in the paint against the towering Valks' defense, and it might be time for her to unlock the next level of her offense.

Although she improved her jumper through the postseason, she still needs to work on turnaround shots, and her efficiency from deep has been underwhelming by her standards.

#2773. Nick Sirianni: Eagles will stick with Tanner McKee, Sean Mannion despite offensive woes

The Eagles have lost six in a row and rank 30th in the NFL in points per game, but Nick Sirianni said Monday that he isn’t making a change at offensive coordinator or quarterback.

Sean Mannion will continue to call plays, and Tanner McKee will remain the starting quarterback with Jalen Hurts out for the year.

“I’m not making any changes there,” Sirianni said about his coaching staff, via Tim McManus of ESPN. “It is on all of us to figure out how to get things going in the right direction. Obviously, right now they’re not. But again, this is the ultimate team game, and we’re in the problem-solving business. Right now, we have to find answers to help us get going offensively. Again, that brunt falls on myself; that falls on Sean; and we’re going to do everything we can to get ourselves out of this.”

The first-year playcaller has had to make do without Hurts, right tackle Lane Johnson, center Cam Jurgens, running back Saquon Barkley and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks at times this season. Hurts played five games before going on injured reserve with blood clots; Johnson retired after three games; Jurgens played four games with the Eagles before a trade to the Ravens; Barkley has missed two games and been limited in others with injuries; Smith has missed four games with a hamstring injury; and Wicks has missed two games with an ankle injury.

The Eagles are averaging 17.1 points a game.

McKee has started the past three games, completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 639 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.

“Tanner’s our guy. We’re not making any changes there,” Sirianni said. “Again, how do we find solutions? That could be within scheme; that could be within how our schedule is, practice plays. Everything’s on the table for us in that aspect. But right now, this is where we are, and we’re trying to find solutions there. We’re looking at everything as far as what we can do differently as coaches.”

McKee’s backup, Joe Milton, only arrived in Philadelphia on Oct. 16, signing from the Cowboys’ practice squad.

#2769. Peyton Manning’s ManningCast prediction backfires on Jaxon Smith-Njigba TD

The Seattle Seahawks have a cheat code on their team: wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. His unique skills allow his team to defy conventional thinking.

Peyton Manning was among the latest to try to apply logic to the Seahawks' logic-defying wideout. During the Week 8 episode of the "ManningCast" on "Monday Night Football," the Hall of Fame quarterback tried to anticipate Seattle's play call as the clock ticked down on the first half.

MONDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL: Seahawks vs Bears score, highlights, analysis

#2764. San Antonio vs. Utah, Final Score: Two impressive Spurs quarters are plenty versus Jazz, 119-97

Behind its dogged dedication on both ends in the first and third periods, San Antonio ran its undefeated streak to five with a 119-97 win over Utah. After conducting a well-played first 12 minutes with balanced contributions, San Antonio held on to that advantage while fending off an extended Jazz run over much of the second quarter. The Spurs then left no doubt after that, as their starters ran the Jazz off the floor in a 35-20 third period.

Dylan Harper (17 points, 8 assists, 7 rebounds, and 2 steals) led the way for San Antonio (5-2) with seven players (and all starters) getting into double figures. Western Conference Player of the Week Victor Wembanyama (12 points, 11 rebounds, 5 assists, and 3 blocks) seemed content to ride shotgun, as Devin Vassell (11 points) carried the offense over many of the team's second quarter minutes, while newly 22-year-old Stephon Castle (16 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists) and De'Aaron Fox (12 points and 3 assists in foul-limited minutes) helped their fellow guards outshine their less experienced Jazz counterparts. Keldon Johnson (15 points and 7 rebounds) was forceful and effective off the bench.

Lauri Markkanen (22 points and 8 rebounds) carried the offense in comparison to Utah's (1-6) callow execution throughout the evening. Jaxson Hayes (9 points and 5 rebounds) and Mo Bamba (8 points and 8 rebounds) provided moments of punch before the Jazz succumbed to the superior Spurs.

All five starters shared well in scoring the team's first 14 points, and the Spurs collectively went up ten early on a sluggish Jazz squad. Utah scores came sparingly throughout the opening frame and their two recent rookie selections combined to go 0-for-8. The Spurs' team defense proved adept both at guiding dribble-drives into the corners away from the rim and crowding the airspace around shooters. San Antonio got in its own way by missing a handful of free throws. All of the impressive two-way execution also was dragged out over a series of referee stoppages throughout the first and yet, the Spurs still left it up 11.

Markkanen found his shooting touch to start the second and helped bring Utah's deficit into single digits. Despite their unrelenting effort to catch and surpass San Antonio, the hosts persevered through many tough minutes throughout the quarter. Vassell and Harper's exploits kept the Spurs afloat, while well-traveled veterans Josh Okogie and Mo Bamba bolstered Markkenen's production. After Wembanyama's tip dunk midway through the second, the non-Wembanyamas fended off Utah 22-15 to make it a 59-49 game at the half.

San Antonio came out of the break intent to prevent any further Utah runs with its trio of Castle, Fox, and Harper doing the bulk of the damage to inflate its lead throughout the third as high as 22. The Spurs, in particular, negated any further support outside of Markkanen in a 35-20 quarter.

"Momma There Go Those Young Men" Sequence: Putting the finishing touches on a San Antonio push over the middle part of the third, Harper nabbed a crosscourt pass, and looked destined to glide in for a lay-up before he lobbed a feather to Castle for a tomahawk jam.

Tarris Reed, Jr. (lithe AND bruising big man) playing time: 3 points and SEVEN rebounds in SEVEN minutes of action!

Wembanyama played nearly 15 feet off of Jaxson Hayes during the initial possession as the Utah center floated outside the paint.

Utah was content to cede Wembanyama the free throw line extended for a good chunk of his first half shot diet to moderate success.

San Antonio's wings helped offset Utah's frontline size in the first half by hitting the defensive boards in droves.

Aside from a quick shooting stroke, there wasn't much that stood out about Peterson. He looked like early-career Buddy Hield out there.

A tussle between Brice Sensabaugh and Harrison Barnes (13 points) was likely not on anyone's scorecard tonight.

Kornet looks heavy-footed when he's going from baseline-to-baseline, but he's playing that dunker spot fairly well.

Sequence of the Game #1: Three-plus minutes in, Wembanyama snagged an errant Jazz miss and, instead of bringing it up himself, floated a 60 foot pass gently into Fox's ready hands for a transition lay-up.

Sequence of the Game #2: Late in the first half, Luke Kornet altered a George three attempt and, moments later, Fox rewarded the center by feeding him for a reverse lay-up at the other end.

Sequence of the Game #3: As part of an opening 10-4 to start the second half, Wembanyama swatted away a George floater, came to a jumpstop short of the paint, and found a streaking Harper for a soaring slam. On the next possession, Harper snared what seemed like a sure turnover on a Wembanyama pass, faked a pass back to his big man, and lofted a floater gently into the net.

Peterson poorly closed out on a Vassell (pronounced by the crew chief as "VASS-ull") corner three and was assessed a Flagrant 1 foul and the Spur guard netted three points from the line. Fox 's straightaway three and Wembanyama's banker put the Spurs up six. Utah's rookie again figured in a referee-involved situation as a shooting foul committed by Castle on Peterson was challenged and overruled. Harper converted a transition lay-up to make it 18-4, and the ensuing foul put Utah in the foul bonus halfway through the stanza. George's second basket came 8+ minutes into the quarter. Will Hardy challenged a Utah foul on a Fox attempt and won it, and Markkanen got the Jazz into double digits 10 minutes in. San Antonio held Utah to its lowest quarterly output of the young season and led 27-16 after one.

Markkanen's pair catch-and-shoot threes at the start of the second quickly brought the Jazz within five. Fox picked up his third foul 50 seconds in. Harper found Johnson crosscourt for an open three and followed that with a triple of his own. Vassell rescued a stalled-out sequence with a late clock jumper. A transition three from Bailey brought Utah within one and their increased aggression drew San Antonio into the foul bonus halfway through the second. Kornet got his first block on a George three, scored a reverse lay-up at the other end, and then set-up Castle for a three to prevent the Jazz from taking the lead. San Antonio built back up its cushion culminating with Johnson's timely pair of lay-ups. Despite Utah's opening push, the Spurs ended the half having lost only one point from their first quarter differential.

Harper and Fox dual-wielded their impressive scoring abilities deep in the paint to start the third, and San Antonio got the lead briefly back up to 16. Coach Johnson called a Pop-like timeout after George scored mere seconds after a Castle make. Markkanen's fourth three stopped the Spurs' momentum briefly. Julian Champagnie missed a straightaway three, secured the miss, and knocked down the next try to push the San Antonio lead to 17. A pair of tips from Markkanen was not nearly enough to dent San Antonio's offensive onslaught. Wembanyama sandwiched a driving lay-up and a lob dunk around a block to make it 94-69 going into the fourth.

Scottie Barnes makes 'terrible' admission after powering Raptors' comeback win vs. Clippers appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Toronto Raptors appeared to be well on their way to suffering a third-consecutive defeat, as they stared at a 13-point deficit heading into the fourth quarter of their Monday night clash against the Los Angeles Clippers. With Kawhi Leonard out, the responsibility to lead the team fell on Scottie Barnes' broad shoulders.

Barnes, however, struggled to the tune of just seven points on 3-of-10 shooting from the field through the first three quarters of play. But in the fourth, the Raptors star came alive. He put up 15 points in the fourth quarter alone, powering Toronto's comeback en route to a 125-118 victory over the Clippers.

After the game, the 25-year-old forward admitted that he was rather "terrible" for most of the Raptors' Monday night game against the Clippers, but he turned it up when it mattered the most and they got the win in the process.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I was terrible for about 29 minutes of this game. Couldn't really figure out what was going on, couldn't really move that well. But then something clicked… I was just trying to fight, get us back in the game… Do whatever it takes to get this win," Barnes said, per Josh Lewenberg of TSN.

The Raptors ended up scoring 47 points in the fourth quarter after scoring just 78 through the first 36 minutes of game time, and a lot of that had to do with Barnes' revival. He was unstoppable near the basket, and this opened up opportunities for the likes of Immanuel Quickley and Collin Murray-Boyles to do damage as well.

The three-point shot deserted Toronto on Monday, as they made just eight of their 29 three-point attempts on the night. But they buckled down on defense, held the Clippers to just 30.4% shooting from the field and forced six turnovers in the fourth, and they converted defense into offense.

Barnes needs to be more assertive and efficient with Leonard out, and the Raptors will look at his fourth quarter display as the blueprint of how he could perform moving forward.

By sending eight-game starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett all the way to No. 3 on the depth chart, the Cardinals have sent a clear message to the rest of the league, eight days from the trade deadline.

The question becomes whether anyone will, and whether based on the games to be played in Week 9 anyone will need to.

Currently, the Ravens are scrambling to find healthy bodies at the position — and quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork was the quarterback coach in Arizona last year, when Brissett started 12 games.

Any other contender could be one snap away from needing Brissett. And the Vikings, who should be (even if they aren’t) thinking about potential upgrades to Kyler Murray, could make the Cardinals a call.

Beyond teams that could be in a position to consider Brissett as the starter are contenders who may not be thrilled with their current primary backups. In L.A., for example, it could make sense to have a more experienced understudy to Matthew Stafford for the stretch run.

Brissett’s new contract had most of the paid out as a signing bonus; his base salary is a very affordable $1.3 million.

Now in his eleventh season, Brissett has played for six teams: the Patriots (twice), the Colts, the Dolphins, the Browns, the Commanders, and the Cardinals. He has 109 regular-season appearances, with 73 starts.

#2753. Chicago Bears solidify standing with Monday night win and Vikings loss

The Chicago Bears were fifth in the NFC coming into Week 8, they fell behind the Detroit Lions on Sunday with their win, and now the Bears are back in the top Wild Card spot after Chicago's Monday night win.

A great development for the Bears is the first loss of the season by the Minnesota Vikings. With Minnesota at 6-1 and the Bears at 6-2, Chicago likely controls their own destiny in the division. A Bears win over the Vikings would give both team two losses and two NFC North losses as well as two NFC losses. It would move the tiebreaker to the Strength of Victory tiebreaker until the Common Games opponents gets to four games, and Chicago would move ahead of Minnesota on the SOV.

In addition to those two NFC North teams winning, the Green Bay Packers won on Thursday night to stick in the seventh and final Wild Card slot. All four NFC North teams are in a playoff spot.

1. San Francisco 49ers (6-1, strength of victory .456)

2. Minnesota Vikings (6-1, strength of victory .400)

10. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5, win over ATL, 1-0 vs DAL+ARZ, 3-2 NFC)

11. Atlanta Falcons (3-5, loss to TB, 3-3 NFC record)

12. Arizona Cardinals (3-5, 1-0 vs DAL+ARZ, 2-4 NFC)

13. Dallas Cowboys (3-5, 0-2 vs TB+ARZ, loss to ARZ)

First, you get to one team per division so the Falcons and Buccaneers are against each other. Tampa has a win over Atlanta, so they have the tiebreaker.

Tampa vs Arizona vs Dallas is a head-to-head tiebreaker where Atlanta and Arizona move on since they both have wins over Dallas. The Bucs are 3-2 in the NFC vs the Cardinals at 2-4, so Tampa is the 10 seed.

Then the Falcons go into a three-way tiebreaker with the Cardinals and Cowboys. It goes straight to NFC record where the Falcons are 3-3 and the Cardinals and Cowboys are 2-4. Atlanta is the 11 seed.

The Arizona Cardinals beat the Cowboys so they win the head-to-head tiebreaker in the two-way decision. Arizona is 12th and the Cowboys are 13th.

#2752. Timberwolves 112, Bucks 100: Ball-ing and Bowling to the Rim

After a grueling week that included five games in seven nights and two back-to-backs, the Timberwolves got back to a normal scheduling rhythm as they kicked off the week against the Milwaukee Bucks. Minnesota took down Milwaukee in a preseason matchup as the Bucks have continued to try to find themselves in their post-Giannis era. They've had a lot of difficulty starting the season, including losing their last two games by 20+ points.

An already depleted Timberwolves roster was down another rotation player in Terrence Shannon Jr., due to a hip contusion, as the injury bug has found its way to the Twin Cities. The border battle clash always provides a little extra fuel, even when the teams are in opposing conferences.

LaMelo Ball, looking frustrated from his recent struggles, came out flame-throwing as the Bucks played drop and allowed him free rein to shoot behind physical Rudy Gobert screens. Ball drove the offense, hitting nothing but nylon on the majority of his shots. He drove the offense for the beginning of the game.

After a half-hearted defensive stretch led to some Bucks triples, Jaylen Clark and Joan Beringer came in and slammed the door. Minnesota kept the defensive intensity up but struggled to put the ball in the hoop after Ball went to the bench, but they maintained a 29-18 advantage after the first 12 minutes.

LaMelo Ball continued to drive the offense as he scored half of their first-half points while being aggressive in looking for his shot. Sloppy rebounding allowed Milwaukee to get back into the game as they closed the gap throughout the quarter.

There were a few stretches where Minnesota lost focus, and it allowed the Bucks to crawl their way back. The sloppiness persisted, and Tyler Herro hit back-to-back threes to close the second as the Bucks sliced into the double-digit Timberwolves advantage and cut the lead to one point.

The Bucks killed the Timberwolves on the glass and created second-chance points. They led that category 16 to 5 at the half.

LaMelo Ball scored 24 points while Jaden McDaniels trailed far behind as the next highest scorer with seven points. Dosunmu filled up the stat sheet in the other categories with seven rebounds and five assists.

Jaden McDaniels started the quarter off on the wrong foot as he got two fouls in the first 20 seconds of the third that sent him to the bench. Ayo Dosunmu took the baton from LaMelo Ball to start the quarter as he was bowling his way to the rim and finishing with feather-like touch. Tyler Herro matched that output as he stayed hot from his close to the second quarter, as the Timberwolves offense sputtered on the other end. The Bucks were getting too easy of looks as the game went back and forth during the period. Trey Lyles also left his mark, scoring 10 points in the third quarter.

It was a close start to the 4th quarter before Joan Beringer and Jaylen Clark gave the Timberwolves a shot in the arm. The Bucks were on a cold streak that Minnesota couldn't seem to shake for much of the game before this point. Those two helped to get some separation and grew the lead to double digits.

Milwaukee decided that they couldn't score with Rudy Gobert out there, nor were they able to stop the Timberwolves' offense, so they deployed the hack-a-Rudy strategy. That somewhat worked for them, as they were able to get Gobert out of the game, but Minnesota battened down the hatches and knocked down a few triples to close out the game for a 112-100 victory.

The Timberwolves themselves were reeling after the Anthony Edwards injury as they did not know who was next up in the team's hierarchy. There were multiple quotes that emphasized this sentiment, but it was always clear who would need to step up with their pack leader sidelined: LaMelo Ball.

Ball struggled initially taking the reins of the team that needed him to have his playmaking take a step back so his shooting could take the shine. He struck that balance in this one. He came out of the gates against the Bucks scorching hot, and kept the pedal down for the entire game.

LaMelo had half of the team's points at halftime and found ways to get his shot off while also finding ways to beat his man off the dribble and take it all the way to the basket. He scored 34 points on 12/21 shooting while adding a 6/13 day from beyond the arc. The fouls almost caught up to him in the second half, but his shooting aggressiveness is exactly what this offense needed.

Ayo Dosunmu is a jack of all trades while being a master at diving at the rim and finishing with a soft touch. While LaMelo was focused on putting the ball in the hoop in this one, Ayo took his role as a facilitator, setting up his fellow Wolves with easy looks all around.

He scored 19 points, added 12 rebounds and 8 assists in a stat-sheet-stuffing night. He is the king of scaling his game up and down to fit whatever the team needs, and did that in the third quarter tonight. When LaMelo was struggling to get going, and the Bucks were fighting back, he calmly took the ball and used his patented straight-line driving and love tapping off the glass to stem the Milwaukee tide.

He is a key part of the Ant-less Timberwolves, and more games where he finds himself all over the court will do the Timberwolves well in this stretch.

The Timberwolves travel south for a matchup against the rugged Houston Rockets (6-1). That game can be streamed on DAZN at 7:30 pm CST.

#2751. Why Bears shouldn’t be NFC Super Bowl favorites despite dominant Jeffery Simmons MNF debut

Why Bears shouldn't be NFC Super Bowl favorites despite dominant Jeffery Simmons MNF debut appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Chicago Bears are making plenty of noise in the NFC. Their latest statement victory has only intensified the championship buzz surrounding the franchise. Adding Jeffery Simmons to an already promising defensive front appears to have given Dennis Allen's unit another dimension. Meanwhile, Caleb Williams continues to demonstrate why Chicago's offensive ceiling is so intriguing. However, one impressive Monday Night Football performance should not automatically make the Bears the favorites to represent the NFC in Super Bowl LXI. Despite their convincing dismantling of the Seattle Seahawks, Chicago still has significant questions to answer. As things stand, the Bears have not yet earned the conference's top billing.

Chicago's statement victory in the Pacific Northwest was undeniably comprehensive. It was a 34-17 dismantling that highlighted both offensive rhythm and defensive resilience. Williams delivered an efficient, mistake-free performance. He threw for 247 yards and a touchdown without committing a single turnover. When Seattle cut the deficit to 20-17 early in the fourth quarter, Chicago responded with ruthless composure. The Bears executed a 39-yard Kalif Raymond reverse before D'Andre Swift capped his three-touchdown night with two late scoring plunges. Defensively, Dennis Allen's unit held Seattle to a miserable 1-of-11 on third downs. Simmons, Montez Sweat, and Devin Bush wreaked havoc in the backfield before James Lynch picked off Sam Darnold to seal the road triumph.

Hold your horses before declaring them Super Bowl favorites, though. The biggest reason to pump the brakes on Chicago's Super Bowl hype is its inability to establish itself within the NFC North. A sparkling 6-2 overall record looks impressive. However, the Bears remain winless against divisional opponents. They still carry an uncomfortable 0-2 record following losses to the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This division remains one of the conference's toughest environments. Chicago cannot afford to overlook the importance of winning those matchups. The Bears are chasing an undefeated Minnesota team while remaining level with Green Bay. That makes their divisional position considerably less comfortable than their overall record suggests.

Winning the NFC North is not an absolute prerequisite for reaching the Super Bowl, of course. Still, securing a favorable playoff seed could prove invaluable.

The remaining matchups against Minnesota, Green Bay, and the Detroit Lions will provide opportunities to change that narrative. Until then, crowning the Bears conference favorites would be premature.

Simmons' Chicago debut was everything the Bears could have hoped for. His combination of power, explosiveness, and interior disruption immediately made an already dangerous defensive front more imposing. However, the victory against Seattle also exposed a potentially significant weakness that could undermine Chicago's championship ambitions.

Both Grady Jarrett and Kentavius Street exited the contest with concerning lower-body injuries. That will immediately place additional pressure on the defensive tackle rotation. Their availability moving forward could become an important factor.

Simmons is capable of commanding double-teams and disrupting blocking schemes. Even an elite interior defender, though, cannot carry an entire defensive line throughout a demanding season. Without dependable rotation pieces, opposing offenses could increasingly target the interior. That could force Simmons to absorb additional punishment while limiting Allen's ability to maintain a consistent pass rush.

That becomes particularly concerning against teams with powerful rushing attacks and experienced offensive lines. Championship defenses need sufficient depth to remain physically imposing throughout four quarters and an entire postseason.

Chicago must closely monitor its defensive tackle situation and explore reinforcements if the injuries prove significant. Simmons has raised the unit's ceiling, but the supporting cast will determine how high that ceiling really goes.

In addition, the conference still features established championship contenders with considerably stronger postseason pedigrees. The San Francisco 49ers remain an obvious benchmark. Their experienced coaching leadership and familiarity with high-pressure playoff situations give them an advantage.

The Bears have arguably developed one of the conference's more exciting offensive combinations. Williams has shown encouraging command, Swift provides explosive rushing production, and the receiving corps offers multiple ways to attack opposing defenses. Simmons' arrival has also given the defense another legitimate game-wrecker.

However, regular-season dominance and postseason execution are two entirely different challenges. The Bears have yet to demonstrate that they can consistently overcome elite opponents with higher stakes.

San Francisco and other established contenders deserve respect until Chicago proves it can match their consistency when the stakes rise.

There is no denying that the Bears have taken a significant step forward. Their victory over Seattle demonstrated their ability to win on the road and respond when an opponent threatens to change the momentum.

Simmons' arrival could prove transformative. Williams and the offensive supporting cast give Chicago legitimate championship potential. Nevertheless, the divisional record, defensive injury concerns, and lack of postseason validation remain difficult to ignore.

The Bears belong in the NFC championship conversation. That said, they should not be considered the conference's unquestioned favorites just yet. The potential is undeniable, of course. Maybe they'll be favorites sooner rather than later. The championship credentials, however, still need to be earned.

#2749. Harry Kane confirms new Bayern Munich contract is 'extremely close' as Ballon d’Or winner prepares for Atletico Madrid test

Harry Kane has confirmed that he is on the verge of signing a new contract with Bayern Munich, with an official announcement expected in the coming days. The England captain, fresh from being crowned the best player in the world, is ready to commit his future to the Allianz Arena as he enters the final stages of his current deal.

The 33-year-old striker is approaching the conclusion of the initial four-year agreement he signed upon arriving from Tottenham in 2023. Following a stellar campaign featuring 73 goals, two domestic trophies, and a third-place World Cup finish with England, Bayern are eager to secure his services long-term.

The newly crowned Ballon d'Or winner confirmed an extension is now purely a matter of resolving minor legal technicalities. Speaking ahead of a crucial European tie, the forward expressed confidence that negotiations will conclude swiftly.

Addressing the media ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash against Atletico Madrid, the England skipper provided a highly positive update on his future. "I would say it is more [a matter of] days," Kane explained. "There has been good conversations over this weekend and today as well.

"I know I keep saying we are close, but we are extremely close now. Details are just details in every contract. A lot of the bigger stuff has been ironed out and we are happy with, but in every contract there is loads of little things that go into it, small details that in the end the lawyers have to thrash out and figure out.

"So all in all I would say it is more days than weeks. From what I have heard, the conversations have gone well again today and hopefully we will be in a place to do something within the next few days."

Away from the boardroom, Bayern are navigating a chaotic spell. Recent days saw Kane lift the Ballon d'Or before missing a penalty in a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund. The squad is also grappling with the absence of recovering head coach Vincent Kompany and serious injuries to Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry.

"It has been a rollercoaster ride. We have experienced all sorts of emotions," Kane reflected. "I had a fantastic moment winning the Ballon d'Or, but there were also the injuries and Joshua Kimmich's situation [earlier in the season] ... Those were difficult moments. You have to be able to cope with that, sport brings us together. We are missing key players and our coach too, but there are others who can seize this opportunity to show what they're made of."

Despite his individual accolades, the striker prioritises collective glory. "I think I would swap the next Ballon d'Or for a Champions League triumph. The team aspect of the sport is why we all play," he said. "Of course, winning the Ballon d'Or was one of the greatest moments of my life, but winning with Bayern, that would be an absolutely incredible feeling.

"We all want to reach the Champions League final and achieve that great success as a team. At the moment I am still in with a chance of winning both."

Assistant coach Aaron Danks will lead an injury-ravaged Bayern side against Atletico, with late fitness checks required for Michael Olise and Manuel Neuer. The fixture carries significant weight, as Bayern sit 14th and Atletico 16th in the European standings following the Bavarians' recent 2-2 draw with Arsenal.

Knowing the importance of stringing together positive results, Kane issued a rallying cry. "If we can win these next two games - tomorrow night and then in the Bundesliga going into that second international break - we'll be in a really good place," he noted. "And hopefully after that we'll have a couple of players coming back. Until then, we just have to stick together and keep doing what we're doing."

#2748. Sixers Bell Ringer: Widespread effort from starters lifts Sixers past Bulls

Bell Ringer Standings:Tyrese Maxey – 3.5Joel Embiid – 1LeBron James – 1Anfernee Simons – 1Jaylen Brown – 0.5

The Philadelphia 76ers had all five starters score in double-digits and three score more than 20 points in a 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls on Monday night.

The Sixers were almost completely healthy for this one, with the only absences being Dominick Barlow (back) and Ariel Hukporti, who is out for the season. Taking on a struggling Bulls squad that came into Monday 1-5 on the season, they had a golden opportunity to get a comfortable win and maybe even get the starters some rest if they could put it to bed early.

Of course, it can never be too easy. After letting Chicago hang close in the first half, the Sixers finally started to put a little distance between them going into the final frame leading by 11. Philadelphia couldn't seem to fully shake loose until late in the fourth when they extended their lead to 20 with two minutes to play. It would have been nice to gain steadier footing early to get the starters some rest before that point, but I guess we can't be too greedy talking about a now 7-1 team.

Next up, the Sixers will hit the road for three games, the first of which will take them to Detroit to take on the Pistons on Wednesday night.

Until then, let's get to the Bell Ringer. It was a widespread effort, so we have a few options!

VJ Edgecombe: 21 points, 3 rebounds, 5 assists, 1 steal, 1 block

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

To anyone who says that VJ Edgecombe can't thrive in this Sixers' lineup, please watch the first quarter of tonight's game. It was the perfect example of a simple but effective synergy between the sophomore and his new-look squad — VJ fully utilizing his speed in transition to get out ahead with LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey getting their heads up to nail impressive passes to him in stride. Edgecombe took full advantage, shooting 5-for-5 from the floor (1-for-1 from long range) for a floor-leading 11 points in the first frame. And if it ain't broke, don't fix it. LeBron hit another cross-court dime to a pushing Edgecombe to help the boy from Bimini to 15 points on 7-for-7 field goal shooting by halftime.

This is why I never worried about Edgecombe's development in this lineup. Sure, there's only one ball… but when you have passers like James (and Maxey, though to a lesser extent) around you, there will always be opportunities for a speedy, athletic player that is constantly in motion off the ball. Tonight was the perfect example of how he can become borderline uncoverable. And if you move (and finish) like Edgecombe did tonight, one can imagine those opportunities will only become more plentiful as the Sixers continue to solidify their chemistry offensively.

Edgecombe finished Monday night with 21 points on 9-for-12 field goal, 2-for-4 three-point shooting. He also had three rebounds, five assists, a steal and a block.

LeBron James: 15 points, 7 rebounds, 9 assists, 1 steal

LeBron James hit not only one but several passes in this game that I watched on repeat. And he made them look easy. I'm talking multiple full-court bounce passes that hit blazing fast players like VJ Edgecombe perfectly in stride and a number of perfectly timed dimes in the half-court offense working off double (or even triple) teams. I'll be honest, I didn't watch LeBron play night in and night out before he came to Philadelphia… it is an absolute treat to watch the plays he makes for his teammates every single game, with the correct passes at the correct time to the correct players to make the most of each moment. By the time an opponent's shot is in the air, James is already positioning himself to grab the rebound and to be able to make a quick, accurate pass ahead.

It sounds like I'm overstating things, but I genuinely don't think it can be overstated what a facilitator he's been to start this season.

In addition to his nine dimes, LeBron found the time to sink some buckets of his own, chipping in 15 on 6-for-13 field goal shooting. He also pulled in seven rebounds and had a steal. His first triple-double as a Sixer still eludes him for now, but something tells me it won't be too long…

Tyrese Maxey: 26 points, 4 rebounds, 11 assists, 2 steals, 2 blocks

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

Philadelphia rained down MVP chants for Tyrese Maxey when he went to the line at one point tonight… and frankly, they're not crazy. Well, maybe they are, but not for this! Maxey continues to be an absolute baller to start this season, and notably it's coming in different ways and on both ends of the floor. Not only has Maxey's defense been incredibly impressive these first eight games… and not only has he been an absolute scoring powerhouse at times… but he's also taking some clear queues from LeBron James and hitting some monster passes as well.

With such a widespread scoring effort tonight, it didn't have to be all on Maxey's shoulders to chip in 40 points. But even without the overwhelming point total tonight (not that 26 is anything to be ashamed of), it's amazing just how many of the Sixers' points Maxey played a large part in, whether he scored them, assisted on them, or came up with the defensive play that led to them. First, he got his team going early. Then, he was scoring in bunches himself by the fourth.

Maxey finished Monday with a 26-point, 11-assist double-double. He shot 10-for-15 from the floor. He also had four rebounds, two steals and two blocks.

Jaylen Brown: 25 points, 11 rebounds, 5 assists, 1 steal

It was another night of Jaylen Brown just being Jaylen Brown. I'm sounding like a broken record across these Bell Ringers, but it's incredible how much Brown contributes each game in a somewhat quiet manner. It's not the high-flying dunks of VJ Edgecombe or the cross-court passes of LeBron James. It's not always one big spurt of scoring where Brown puts the Sixers on his back for a few minutes. It's just simple, constant contribution when he's on the floor, on both ends of the floor. You hear his name called by Matt Cord in the arena so often you almost stop hearing it. He just balls. Tonight, it was 25 points on stellar shooting, 9-for-15 field goal and 4-for-7 from beyond the arc, spread out pretty evenly throughout the entirety of the game. This level of performance has seemingly already become the accepted, unceremonious norm from Brown on the Sixers… and that's something worth taking note of.

Brown finished the night with a 25-points, 11-rebounds (5 offensive) double-double with 5 assists and 1 steal. He hit four triples, two of which game back-to-back late in the game which really felt like the dagger in this one (finally).

#2747. Seahawks-Bears score: 4-4. Seahawks blown out in Monday night horror show

All the good feelings the Seattle Seahawks (4-4) brought back after dominating the Kansas City Chiefs were immediately canceled out and then some after a disappointing 34-17 home loss against the Chicago Bears (6-2). Caleb Williams was as brilliant as Sam Darnold was worryingly atrocious. This offense is Jaxon Smith-Njigba or nothing. The run game struggled even with the return of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price. Seattle's vaunted defense had some wins and some devastating losses against the high-flying Bears offense, which looks like a Super Bowl caliber unit. Chicago had 363 yards of total offense, the most by any Seahawks opponent this season, while Seattle had a meager 252. As usual, JSN had 118 of those 252 yards.

Seattle won the Super Bowl last season and it should be cherished forever. This year's team is not a lock for the playoffs. It is not playing complementary football and the sloppiness is too hard to gloss over. It's a disappointing first half of the season and the longer term outlook on this team is significantly altered by the continued struggles of Sam Darnold. How can you have a contender when the quarterback play is this shaky? Whether Brian Fleury is good or not, Darnold is a problem. A big problem.

The Seahawks offense has threatened a blowout loss all season with their erratic play. It finally happened. The defense cannot bail you out forever.

The Seahawks started on offense, giving Zach Charbonnet the ball in his first touch since January 2026. Sam Darnold was rocked for a hurried incomplete pass on 2nd and 5, then Tory Horton was leveled by Cam Lewis on 3rd and 5 in a very legal and physical collision. Seattle had Chicago pinned at the 2-yard line, if not for Rodney Thomas ridiculously sliding for no reasons and driving the ball into the end zone. Poor decision and costly for field position reasons.

Chicago's opening drive against the league's top-rated defense was a thing of beauty. Caleb Williams led a 17-play, 80-yard drive that included three conversions on 3rd down, as well as a D'Andre Swift 4th and 1 conversion to keep the series going. Luther Burden capped off an 8:32 drive with a touchdown grab on a rollout throw by Williams. That was impressive. 7-0 Bears.

Jeffery Simmons made an immediate impact in his Bears debut, sacking Sam Darnold on the first play of Seattle's second series. However, Grady Jarrett's silly face mask grab of Jalen Sundell resulted in a free 15 and a new set of downs. Seattle still didn't get a first down on its own, with Darnold sliding and getting jarred by former Seahawks linebacker Devin Bush. Somehow, this wasn't deemed a penalty, and Seattle punted.

Luckily, Irv Charles showed everyone how its done and downed a Dickson punt inside the 5. The Bears went three-and-out after Caleb Williams was pressured into an overthrow of Kalif Raymond. Tory Taylor's short punt had a short return by Tory Horton, but Seattle was near midfield nevertheless.

When in doubt, go to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. A couple of quick screens to JSN gained 35 yards and Seattle was in the red zone in next to no time. Jadarian Price's first carry back from injury gained eight yards, a promising sign for his health and explosiveness. Unfortunately, the red zone series was ugly and featured nothing but Charbonnet touches that didn't get Seattle particularly close to the end zone. Jason Myers put Seattle on the board with a 27-yard field goal. 7-3 Bears.

The Bears went three-and-out again, then the Seahawks looked like they had a huge special teams play from Irv Charles. He deflected a Tory Taylor punt and somehow it took a friendly, untouched bounce for 45 yards. Seattle went three-and-out and punted it back to the Bears.

Chicago added to its lead thanks to a big play-action shot to Luther Burden for 23 yards. It took only three plays for Seattle to get into field goal range, where the drive stalled. Cairo Santos was true from 44 yards. 10-3 Bears.

Another three-and-out resulted in nervous energy from the Lumen Field crowd. The Bears had a chance to double up with points before the half and then to start the second half. Williams again was on target with explosive plays, as Rome Odunze broke free for 24 yards after a long time for Caleb Williams in the pocket. Interestingly enough, Ben Johnson dialed up a D'Andre Swift run on 3rd and 6 on the other side of the two-minute warning. Swift gained four yards and set up 4th and 2. Johnson called for the hard count, which was unsuccessful, and then kicked another field goal. 13-3 Bears.

A Jaylon Johnson PI penalty gifted Seattle some free yards in their one-minute drill. JSN broke Jaylon Johnson's ankles two plays later to get into Chicago territory. On 3rd and 10, Darnold dialed up a deep shot to JSN for a wide open 43-yard touchdown. Tyrique Stevenson bit on the slant and there was no safety help, so you know the rest! The only bad thing was a horrific missed PAT by Jason Myers. 13-9 Bears at halftime.

The Bears and Seahawks traded punts out of halftime, but Chicago punished Seattle for yet another limp three-and-out. A 10-play, 69-yard drive took over six minutes off the clock. D'Andre Swift punched it in from a couple yards out to make it 20-9 Bears.

Seattle took a preposterous 6:29 to move slowly, barely effectively, and not score any points. A very iffy pass interference penalty on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the first of his entire career, took away a completed ball to the Chicago 1. That put the Seahawks behind the sticks, and inevitably they settled for a field goal. Jason Myers' 33-yard kick was blocked. Brutal.

But wait! A twist on the next drive! Caleb Williams was almost picked off by Julian Love on an overthrow, then sacked by Mike Morris for the first of Mike's career, and a give-up screen on 3rd and 20 was fumbled by Colston Loveland. DeMarcus Lawrence forced the fumble and recovered the ball all at once!

Seattle turned that turnover into points, but not without referee help. Darnold was picked off on a terrible double coverage throw, but Clark Phillips was called for a hold of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and that took away the turnover. Two plays later, Darnold hit an open Cooper Kupp for a touchdown. Tory Horton kept the feet down in the back of the end zone for two valuable points. 20-17 Bears with 11:46 to go.

A really awful penalty committed by Mike Morris resulted in great field position for the Bears on the ensuing kick return. Seattle still had a chance to get the Bears off the field on third down in fringe field goal range. A delay of game actually saved the Bears from a failed 3rd and 4 conversion. On 3rd and 9, a screen to the speedy Kalif Raymond broke through for a 39-yard gain and it officially goes down as a run. D'Andre Swift scored on the next play. 27-17 Bears.

Sam Darnold got picked in an impossibly funny way. He was aloof and didn't realize the ball was picked by James Lynch. D'Andre Swift got the game-sealing hat trick after Nick Emmanwori selfishly committed a personal foul penalty when the Bears had 3rd and goal. 34-17 Bears FINAL.

DL Leonard Williams left the game in the third quarter with a stinger and did not return.

C Jalen Sundell left the game in the fourth quarter with an undisclosed injury.

The Seahawks wrap up their three-game homestand against the Arizona Cardinals (3-5) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1:25 pm PT on FOX. Unlike the first meeting, the Cardinals will have Gardner Minshew II at QB instead of Jacoby Brissett.

#2745. Rapid Recap: Timberwolves 112, Bucks 100

After fighting for most of the game, the Milwaukee Bucks stalled late, letting the Minnesota Timberwolves ride a dominant final four minutes to a 112-100 win. The Bucks slump to 1-6 for only the fifth time in franchise history, extending their losing streak to three games. Tyler Herro led the Bucks in scoring, posting 21 points on 8/18 shooting. Jaime Jaquez scored 19 and added eight rebounds, while Myles Turner and AJ Green each added 13 points. LaMelo Ball led all players with a season-high 34 points on 12/21 shooting, while Ayo Dosunmu (19 points, 12 rebounds, eight assists) had a near triple-double.

Taylor Jenkins tweaked his rotation on Monday, dropping Ryan Rollins from the starting lineup in favor of Brayden Burries. Kyle Kuzma fired a bullet to an open Jaime Jaquez in the paint, who easily rolled it in for a layup to start the scoring. However, led by back-to-back long threes from LaMelo Ball, the Wolves rattled off 10 unanswered points to take an eight-point lead inside the first three minutes. Ball connected on his third triple of the game with just four minutes elapsed, putting the Timberwolves up 15-4 and forcing a Bucks timeout. Milwaukee quickly worked their way back out of the break, going on a 9-0 run behind triples from Jaquez, Burries, and Myles Turner; Burries showed the hustle to compete with bigger Wolves defenders on the offensive glass and consistently found teammates on the perimeter. The Wolves responded with a run of their own (12-3), scoring ten points and feasting in transition to lead 29-18 after one.

Impressively, Milwaukee quickly cut the Timberwolves' lead out of the break and even took the lead, with AJ Green connecting on a pair of threes, Rollins getting a driving layup to go, and Burries converting a pull-up. However, Ball caught fire once again, helping Minnesota take the lead right back; the Wolves' star PG scored 11 second-quarter points on 4/7 shooting, and his presence created so many good looks. However, the Bucks did one thing well: they took away Ball's passing game, with his first assist coming with 1:40 remaining in the third quarter. Anyway, Ball's and-one gave Minnesota a 45-41 lead with 2:51 remaining, but Milwaukee kept it tight, with Herro cashing back-to-back threes in the final minute to cut the home side's lead to one, 48-47, at the half.

Although Minnesota stayed in control for much of the third quarter, Milwaukee kept the game within arm's reach. Myles Turner's triple off a Kuzma kick-out gave Milwaukee a 50-48 lead to start, but Minnesota wrenched it back with an Ayo Dosumnu fast-break layup. Bones Hyland's three gave Minnesota a 68-63 lead with just under five minutes left. Milwaukee and Minnesota kept trading the lead as the game wore on. Trey Lyles gave the home side a nice kick off the bench, knocking down a few bombs late in the third to give Minnesota a 76-71 edge. The Wolves stayed ahead going into the final frame, though a tough Kasparas Jakucionis finish through contact cut their lead to just four at 80-76.

Minnesota slowly built its advantage as the fourth quarter wore on, with Milwaukee struggling with turnovers as they tried to bridge the gap; Joan Beringer intercepted a bad Jakucionis pass, another Jakucionis pass went out of bounds, and Turner lost the ball while trying to draw a foul. These mistakes let the Wolves slowly build a double-digit lead, punctuated by Beringer's put-back layup that forced a Jenkins timeout. Eventually, Milwaukee's offense flatlined as Minnesota picked up steam: Kuzma airballed a three and Kel'el Ware missed a dunk, while a Ball dagger pushed the T-Wolves' lead to 15, their largest of the game. Despite trying some interesting tactics to close the game—including hack-a-Rudy—the Bucks just didn't have enough.

The Bucks shot 30.6% from three-point range, highlighted by an ugly first quarter where they went 3/18 and a fourth quarter where they shot 2/9. The Bucks finished second in three-point shooting percentage (38.9%) last year, and they don't look close to matching that this year.

Brayden Burries needs to start from here on out. The rookie got his first start tonight over Ryan Rollins, who has struggled mightily this season (and was bad tonight, shooting 4/11 with three turnovers). And to be clear, Burries was far from perfect, managing just nine points on 4/15 shooting, but his physical defense and rebounding really stood out.

"I'm happy. I think the most important thing was our mentality. After the last game [3-2 DFB-Pokal win] against Bremen, we were not so happy about our performance then.

"The coach said it was not our best game and we agreed. We tried to change the mentality and show we are here to fight for titles and we are not afraid of any team," he said.

Netting in the 89th-minute to salvage a point for the Westphalians, the Portuguese striker said being a substitute frustrates him but working for the team matters most.

"It feels important to help the team. Football is not only about goals. I was there to help the team and try create chances for teammates. I also combine with Serhou [Guirassy] well.

"Of course I want to be on the pitch from the start. If I say I'm happy to start on the bench, then I would not be 100 percent honest with you. At first I am of course angry.

"But I try to always be positive because I know I am important for the team. If I start on the pitch or bench, I focus on that because we have an amazing squad to fight for titles," he concluded.
